title: Etale localization of the ambient adjoint
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring. Use the ordinary unbounded derived categories $D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ of constant-ring module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. For a separated etale morphism $u:U\to X$ of finite type [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], etale sum extension $u_!$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension] is exact on sheaves, and its termwise derived functor is left adjoint to $u^*$ on these whole derived categories. For the compact-support assertion assume in addition that $A$ is finite. If $f:X\to S$ and $fu:U\to S$ are compactifiable morphisms between Noetherian schemes [def-asd-compactifiable, def-amb-etale-compact-support], and $f^\times,(fu)^\times$ denote their ordinary etale compact-support right adjoints [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint], then for every $K\in D(S_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ there is a canonical natural isomorphism
$$u^*f^\times K\cong(fu)^\times K.$$
The notation refers only to ordinary etale compact supports.

proof.text: Reuse the exact sheaf sum-extension/restriction adjunction and its existing termwise unbounded derived adjunction derivedEtaleLowerShriekUpperStarAdjunction. These are the first assertion; no reconstruction via stalks or bounded truncations is needed.

proof.text: Prove that the canonical sheaf arrow from a compactification candidate to direct image is monic. For an open immersion j, the localization functor is fully faithful. At a test object V its left-Kan-extension indexing category is empty, or has a terminal object whose structure arrow is invertible: a lift of V gives V itself as an object over the open. Thus a presheaf arrow out of j-presheaf-extension is monic whenever its transpose is monic. In the empty case its source is zero; in the terminal-object case its component is the transpose composed with isomorphisms. Apply sheafification, which preserves monomorphisms, and use the sheafification adjunction to conclude the same for sheaves. The transpose of j_!F to j_*F is the inverse restriction/direct-image counit, by the triangle identity, so the comparison is monic. Direct image preserves monomorphisms; postcomposing its image with the direct-image composition isomorphism proves the assertion for every compactification.

proof.text: For two normalization families N and Nprime, their sheafComparison arrows have the same composite with the preceding monomorphism by sheaf_normalization. Cancel it objectwise to obtain equality of the sheaf arrows. Their comparison inverses agree on every homotopy representative by derived_normalization. Precomposition with the localization Qh is faithful on natural transformations, so their inverse natural transformations, and hence their comparison isomorphisms, are equal. This establishes equality of comparisons, without choosing arbitrary data from an existence theorem.

proof.text: Use the unchanged definition etaleAmbientLeftComparison. For c compactifying f and d compactifying u followed by f, form d.ofComp c. Whisker the inverse normalized comparison for its restriction with the c candidate; compose with rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactificationCompIso and rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactificationIso. These existing unbounded constructors already implement the proper/open exchange, open-extension composition, derived direct-image composition and common-refinement comparison, so there is no bounded-below telescope argument in this module.

proof.text: Take a witness Nzero from nonempty_etaleCompactSupportNormalization in the theorem proof. Compose the derived sum-extension adjunction with the supplied adjF, and transport its left functor through etaleAmbientLeftComparison for Nzero. This gives an adjunction of the d candidate with F followed by derived restriction. Apply Mathlib Adjunction.rightAdjointUniq to this adjunction and adjG. Mathlib rightAdjointUniq_hom_app_counit, the formula for ofNatIsoLeft_counit and the composite-counit formula give exactly the stated normalization. Step 3 replaces Nzero by every N. For uniqueness, apply the inverse homEquiv of adjG objectwise: the stated equation at Nzero forces the same transpose and hence the same components. Natural-transformation and isomorphism extensionality give uniqueness. The construction is the displayed Hom-bijection/Yoneda argument, with its specified counit.

theorem existsUnique_etaleAmbientAdjointLocalityIso
    (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A] [Finite A]
    {U X S : Scheme.{u}} (u : U ⟶ X) (f : X ⟶ S)
    [Etale u] [IsSeparated u] [LocallyOfFiniteType u] [QuasiCompact u]
    [IsNoetherian U] [IsNoetherian X] [IsNoetherian S]
    (c : Compactification f) (d : Compactification (u ≫ f))
    (F : DerivedCategoryModule A S ⥤ DerivedCategoryModule A X)
    (G : DerivedCategoryModule A S ⥤ DerivedCategoryModule A U)
    (adjF : rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactification (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) c ⊣ F)
    (adjG : rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactification (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) d ⊣ G) :
    ∃! e : F ⋙ (upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) u).mapDerivedCategory ≅ G,
      ∀ (N : EtaleCompactSupportNormalization A) (K : DerivedCategoryModule A S),
        (rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactification (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) d).map
            (e.hom.app K) ≫ adjG.counit.app K =
          (etaleAmbientLeftComparison A N u f c d).inv.app
              ((upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) u).mapDerivedCategory.obj (F.obj K)) ≫
            (rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactification (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) c).map
              ((derivedEtaleLowerShriekUpperStarAdjunction
                (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) u inferInstance).counit.app (F.obj K)) ≫
            adjF.counit.app K

The theorem uniquely characterizes the natural locality isomorphism by its counit transpose, for arbitrary compactifications and adjunctions, simultaneously for every graph-normalized comparison family (whose existence is recorded on lem-asd-etale-compact-support-normalization). C3 proved the remaining theorem on 2026-10-18: private, fully proved Kan-extension helpers establish comparison uniqueness; the existing composite adjunction and Mathlib right-adjoint uniqueness supply the counit-normalized unique isomorphism. blueprint_update.statement:
For a separated etale morphism $u:U\to X$ of finite type,
$u_!$ is exact and is left adjoint to $u^*$ on the whole
ordinary derived categories. If $f$ and $fu$ are
compactifiable, there is a canonical isomorphism

$$
u^*f^\times K\cong(fu)^\times K.
$$

proof.text:
An etale morphism is a local homeomorphism of etale topoi.
For an etale test object $V\to X$, the sheaf $u_!F$
consists of sections on $U\times_XV$ with support proper
over $V$; after an etale covering which separates any finite
set of support points, this is the direct sum of the sections on
the corresponding sheets. This description is independent of
the covering by sheaf descent. It gives
$(u_!F)_{\bar x}=\bigoplus_{\bar z\in U_{\bar x}}F_{\bar z}$,
so $u_!$ is exact. Maps from these sums to $G$ are
precisely maps $F\to u^*G$, first on separated sheets and
then by sheaf descent. Thus $u_!\dashv u^*$ already on
sheaves. Both functors are exact, so the adjunction descends
termwise to ordinary derived categories.

For any complex $M$ on $U$, use the ambient adjunction
of [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint] and the composition
of compact supports in [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons]:

$$
\begin{split}
\operatorname{Hom}_U(M,u^*f^\times K)
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X(u_!M,f^\times K)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_S(Rf_!u_!M,K)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_S(R(fu)_!M,K).
\end{split}
$$

Yoneda gives the displayed isomorphism and its compatibility
with units, counits, and further etale localization.
